rationale: This is simply the MIN-intersection of two already-evaluated archive signals (CashCapexRunwayValue and CashValueNoDilution), introducing no new variable or mechanism while further shrinking coverage, so it is a redundant recombination rather than a test of a new idea.

Adding asset vintage to the already-tested CashFundedCapexValue gate is a coherent and internally consistent refinement of the harvesting mechanism, though the vintage leg previously produced wrong-signed FF5 alpha and the triple gate will push coverage below 0.08, so the incremental payoff is uncertain.

The acquisition-restraint channel is economically distinct from the capex/dilution conditioners already tested and the expression matches the stated sign, but the heavy mass of zero aqc means the conditioning leg ties at the top for most firms and the signal may largely degenerate into plain cash-to-price.

This uses exactly the same three ingredients as the archived PriceyCashBurnAcquirer with only the aggregation operator changed from product to MIN gate, a structure already demonstrated on the same cash-burn theme by PriceyHiringCashBurnGate, so it is close to a mechanical rediscovery rather than a new mechanism.

The expression is internally consistent and the debt-financing leg is a genuinely different funding channel from the archived equity-issuance version, but it is a single-ingredient swap that also overlaps substantially with the well-documented net-external-financing and asset-growth anomalies.

The asset-vintage leg (ppent/ppegt) is near-mechanically implied by sustained heavy capex, making it largely redundant with the capex-deficit leg, and this same vintage conditioner already produced a wrong-signed FF5 alpha in PriceyFreshCapacityUnderuse, so the expected negative sign is poorly supported.
